question: Is the Chez native front end (source -> staged unit -> descriptors -> Core) faster than the BEAM's on the SDK's own units, per unit, same SDK, same units?
summary: Native is slower, not faster: 349.8 s against 256.4 s over the same 667 units (BEAM/native 0.73 of totals), median unit 316.8 ms against 184.5 ms (per-unit ratio median 0.54, p10 0.40, p90 1.00). Native is faster on 66 of 667 units and at least 2x faster on 20. The go bar was native >= 2x faster per unit. Descriptors and Core terms are =:= the BEAM's for 664 of 668 units.

sdk.note: main's current SDK when the runs started; every step used it (the BEAM step through that SDK's own bin/bl), although main's current SDK moved to vdd8ppw... during the runs

native_image.base: research/native-seed/out/chez-main, derived with --base f4e4cec5c (the N2b host edits) plus this branch's two host edits (host/native-data-bifs.scm host/n0-now-us/0, host/native-refusals.scm native-front-refusals)
native_image.compiled_in: lower-core and lower (the SDK's priv/boot), native-front.hook, host.record and host.aot (the SDK's host/aot.bl with compile_descriptor hooked, the 9 definitions stage.bl replaces cut, then loader-decls, front-end/stage.bl and front-end/n0/driver.bl), appended by qualify.bl candidate --additions; boot units core, compiler and host.compiler refreshed to the SDK's sources
what_compiling_needed: every :remote a compiled unit names must link to a compiled definition or a host leaf (native.bootstrap/remote-decision); an evaluated file resolved them at call time. 126 such keys (listed by front-end/n0/remotes.bl) are named refusals, failing at their call as the evaluated call did; function_exported answers false for them as before
host.aot's require closure must hold lower, native-front.hook and host.record (the evaluated copy reached them by load order)
the image's core has no `vector` (an evaluated call found one at run time); host.aot gets a private one
main's priv/boot postdates chez-main: core names BeamLisp.Env/namespaces/0 and the compiler BeamLisp.Loader/ns_home/1 (refused; not reached by staging)

method.native: one Chez process (qualify.bl eval on the candidate image) stages every unit of the SDK's unit index in a real constructor context (front-end/stage.bl nf-unit), then lowers every descriptor and generated descriptor to Core (lower/module->core). Timed per unit with Chez's monotonic clock (host/n0-now-us). native front-to-Core = stage + lower; the ETF writes and the forced major collection nf-memo-recount! makes between units are reported apart and not counted.
method.beam: one fresh VM of the SDK's own bl (--cold): per unit AOT/open_workspace + prepare_unit + close_workspace! (as compare.bl and unit-store.bl), then lower/module->core over the plans' descriptors. prepare_unit compiles a unit's generated modules to beams inside itself; that compile is timed again on the same descriptors (BeamLisp.Emit/compile_descriptor) and removed, and their module->core added. BEAM front-to-Core = prepare - generated beam compile + core + generated core. Timed with erlang:monotonic_time(microsecond).
method.runs: native 4 corpus runs, BEAM 3; runs 2-4 / 1-3 ran in pairs at the same time (two batch slots), so each pair saw the same load. A unit's time is its median over runs.
method.identity: each BEAM run checks the native descriptors =:= its own and the native Core =:= module->core of its own descriptor

load_average_1min.pairs: native 2 with beam 1, native 3 with beam 2, native 4 with beam 3 ran at the same time; native 1 ran alone
load_average_1min.host: 16 cores, 15.7 GB, single-threaded runs under work run --memory 4G

custody_per_unit.what: AOT/ns_closure_hash, AOTCache/key_for_ns and the sha256 of the source (front-end/custody.bl)
custody_per_unit.note: timed per unit on the BEAM with its own source snapshot; custody.bl's single pass over all 668 units took 3.3-4.3 s wall in a warm VM

kernel.what: front-end/kernel.bl: the constructor kernel (boot manifest, Core seed rows, C++ alias rows, phase libraries) as data
kernel.note: a cold VM including its start, 5.47-5.58 s over three captures

accounting_native_needs_from_beam.declaration_tables_and_beam_md5s: carried in custody.etf, computed once per SDK with the custody pass

generated_module_md5_round_trip.note: a unit whose plan generates class or actor modules embeds each one's MD5, which only a BEAM compile answers; the 75 such units are staged twice, so they cost about twice their native time plus the BEAM compile

warm_compile.what: one unit staged and lowered again in the already-running compiler, five repeats after the corpus pass (the first repeat dropped); the BEAM side also runs Compiler/eval_string of the same source under a fresh namespace (read, compile, load, run: the path a changed project file takes)
warm_compile.tiny_unit: reload.preinit-counter, 168 bytes, four lines: native 91.0 ms median (min 84.0), BEAM prepare_unit 53.3 ms (min 50.1), BEAM eval_string 36.4 ms (min 34.0)
warm_compile.note: the ~2 ms a project edit pays today is eval_string of a file without its own namespace work; a four-line namespace already costs 34-39 ms on the BEAM's own path. The native staging path has a floor of 84-104 ms per unit (smallest_20_median_ms, warm tiny unit) against the BEAM prepare_unit's ~50 ms, so a native compile service would raise, not lower, what a project edit pays. auth.audit's eval_string was refused in the measuring VM (sdk_native_library_outside_selected_sdk: the worktree's priv/native/datom_vector), so it has no eval_string row.

earlier_numbers.n2b_evaluated_harness: 745 s for 666 units on SDK nhrajw (front-end/run.sh, aot.bl evaluated at run time, writes and GC included)
earlier_numbers.this_run_compiled: UNITS-DONE 412.7 / 413.3 / 418.8 / 427.9 s for 668 units with writes and GC (front-to-Core alone 348.6-361.4 s): compiling the front end into the image is about 1.8x faster than evaluating it, and still slower than the BEAM

why_no_go: the bar was native >= 2x faster per unit on real units; measured per-unit median ratio 0.54 (native 1.86x slower) and totals 0.73 (1.36x slower)
it holds across sizes: every size quartile has native 1.7-2.1x slower at the median (by_size_quartile)
both the fixed cost and the slope are worse or equal: least-squares 144 ms + 28.7 ms/KB native against 142 ms + 18.3 ms/KB BEAM; the 20 smallest units take 104 ms native against 53 ms
lowering alone (lower/module->core, the same BL code on both) is 18.4 s native against 14.5 s BEAM, so this is the native runtime, not the staging harness
the native path still needs the BEAM for custody (13.4 s), the kernel (5.5 s per SDK) and a second pass for the 75 units that generate modules (55 s), none of which is in the native number above
to reach go the native front end needs about 3.7x on the median unit (0.54 -> 2.0); no measured native optimisation so far moved the reader job by more than a few per cent (C1, C2)
